APCTT-C01.quote: The PRMS simulations are based on the spatial variation in measurable physical characteristics, including land cover, topography, soil, and geology, that can be quantified using geographic information systems (GISs).
APCTT-C01.note: Physical basis of the watershed model, with citations (p16).

APCTT-C02.quote: The report documents a watershed scale hydrologic model that is used to assess the effects of climate change on hydrologic responses and vulnerability.
APCTT-C02.note: Application: vulnerability assessment for the State's climate action plan.

APCTT-C03.quote: Based on evidence from the five models used to evaluate hydrologic change in four representative watersheds, stream-flow is likely to increase in New Hampshire.
APCTT-C03.note: Simulation results showing the models' key function.

APCTT-C05.quote: The results show that the mean simulated daily streamflow for the 31-year calibration period matches the USGS measured streamflows within -12 to 17 percent, with an average difference for all four basins of 6 percent.
APCTT-C05.note: Calibration against measured streamflow at 45 gages and evaluation of four basin models (NSE, NRMSE).

APCTT-C06.quote: The study uses output from general circulation models to drive hydrologic simulations of streamflow, groundwater base flow (hereafter referred to as base flow), and snowfall in four representative watersheds in New Hampshire during the 21st century, including the watersheds of the Ashuelot, Oyster, Pemigewasset, and Souhegan Rivers.
APCTT-C06.note: The calibrated models were applied to future scenarios for the real watersheds.

APCTT-C07.note: Described as a test case; no operational use.

APCTT-C10.note: Differences are compared with other PRMS studies (p22), not with stated requirements.

APCTT-C11.quote: The daily precipitation and air temperature data used for this model were obtained through the USGS Geo Data Portal (http://cida.usgs.gov/gdp/) for a 32-year calibration period (1980–2011) and for future climate datasets consisting of 20-year time periods.
APCTT-C11.note: Inputs, calibration period, scenarios and time slices described.

APCTT-C12.quote: This study is a test case to assemble the information and create the tools to assess the hydrologic vulnerabilities in four specific watersheds.
APCTT-C12.note: Evidence concerns the four-watershed climate-response models.

notes: Agrees with the organizer estimate TRL 6.
